title: Deep anterior lamellar keratoplasty versus penetrating keratoplasty: comparison of clinical outcomes in contralateral eyes

indication: Contralateral eyes of 26 patients (keratoconus 19, stromal dystrophy 6, post-LASIK ectasia 1): PK in the eye with Descemet membrane rupture (hydrops history, opacities) or deep dystrophic lesions, big-bubble DALK in the fellow eye; normal preoperative IOP, no ocular comorbidity; eyes with at least 3 years of follow-up

groups.description: Penetrating keratoplasty: Barron vacuum trephine 7.00-8.25 mm, donor 0.25 mm larger, 10-0 nylon interrupted or combined sutures; eye-bank donors in Eusol-C; moxifloxacin 10 days, dexamethasone then loteprednol, topical steroid for 18-24 months; one surgeon, 2010-2017, retrospective

Deep anterior lamellar keratoplasty (Anwar big-bubble technique) in the contralateral eye of the same patients, donor endothelium stripped, same suturing; topical steroid for 12-18 months; host Descemet membrane and endothelium retained

exclusions.what: Tables 1-3 (refraction, endothelial cell density and loss) and IOP in Figure 3

notes: Two standard keratoplasty techniques compared in contralateral operated eyes of the same patients without an investigational agent; both recorded as control with per-group procedure (pk, dalk). The arms are not independent samples and the contralateral eye is an operated arm, not an unoperated fellow eye.
Procedure allocation followed disease features (PK for Descemet rupture/hydrops or deep lesions), not randomization.
The preoperative reference is the recipient (mostly keratoconic) cornea; postoperative CCT includes the donor graft (full thickness in PK, anterior lamella over host Descemet membrane in DALK).

Inclusion required at least 3 years of follow-up (selection by follow-up length, not by a postoperative outcome). Examinations were also done at 1 day, 1 week, 1 and 3 months, but Table 4 reports only the listed times.
Microperforation occurred in 4 DALK eyes without conversion; 3 DALK eyes had a double anterior chamber resolved with air on day 1; no graft failure or rejection.
